[MUQATIL:35:21-24/r2] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The living are believers and the dead are unbelievers; sight and blindness, light and darkness, and life and death picture believer and unbeliever.
[MUQATIL:35:21-24/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | God causes whom He wills to hear faith.

[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r1] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The contrasts of seas, sight, darkness and light, shade and heat, and life and death all picture the difference between believer and unbeliever.

[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p784#2/r4] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | Believers are alive in religion, as in 6:122, where God gives life through faith. | mentions 6:122
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r1] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The dead are the unbelievers in religion.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r2] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | God makes those whom He wills hear by guiding them to faith.
[YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p785/r3] YAHYA-SALLAM, d. 200 · author | holds | The Prophet cannot make unbelievers accept guidance; they are like the dead, who do not hear those in this world.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p361#4/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | The living and the dead are a comparison for intelligent and ignorant people.
[TAB-FULL:v19p357/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Living hearts believe in God and His Messenger and know revelation; dead hearts overwhelmed by disbelief cannot understand God's commands or distinguish guidance from error. The contrasts portray belief and disbelief.
[TAB-FULL:v19p357/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says blindness, darkness, heat, and death portray disobedience; sight, light, shade, and life portray obedience.
[TAB-FULL:v19p357/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatada describes believers as alive in effect, sight, intention, and action, while disbelievers are dead in sight, heart, and action.
[TAB-FULL:v19p357/r4] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · ابن زيد | reports | Ibn Zayd says the believer sees his religion while the disbeliever is blind; the living person given light represents guidance into Islam, unlike the blind heart in darkness. | mentions 6:122
[TAB-FULL:v19p359/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | As the dead in graves cannot hear scripture and be guided, the Prophet cannot make spiritually dead people benefit from admonition, proofs, or revelation.
[TAB-FULL:v19p359/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says the disbeliever neither hears nor benefits from what he hears.
[IBNABIHATIM:v10p3179#3/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says the unbeliever, like someone in a grave, neither hears nor benefits from what he hears. He adds that every community had a messenger from God, and that earlier messengers brought proofs, scriptures, and a clear Book; God swiftly punished their deniers in this world and then consigned them to the Fire. | mentions 35:24, 35:25, 35:26
[NAHHAS:v3p369/r1] NAHHAS, d. 338 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas identifies living and dead as believers and unbelievers, darkness and light as error and guidance, and shade and heat as paradise and fire.
[NAHHAS:v3p369/r2] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الأخفش سعيد | reports | Al-Akhfash says لا is extra, so darkness and light, shade and heat are simply not equal.
[NAHHAS:v3p369/r3] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | prefers | One view restricts حرور to night and سموم to day; the preferred view allows حرور at either time because its intensive form denotes harmful heat.
[NAHHAS:v3p369/r4] NAHHAS, d. 338 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan reads without tanwin on مسمع for ease; the dead are like those who do not benefit from or accept what they hear.
[THALABI:v8p104#2/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The living are believers and the dead are unbelievers; God enables whom He wills to hear, take admonition, and respond, while the Prophet cannot make unbelievers hear, for they are like the dead.
[THALABI:v8p104#2/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · أشهب العقيلي | reports | Ashhab al-Uqayli reads بمسمع without nunation, construing it in an annexation.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r6] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | Blind and seeing, darkness and light, shade and heat, and living and dead are unlike states and cannot be equated.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r7] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · author | holds | The contrasts signify those joined to God versus distracted from Him, drawn near versus veiled, chosen versus forsaken, and made witnesses versus heedless.
[QUSHAYRI:v3p66/r8] QUSHAYRI, d. 465 · منشدون | reports | An anonymous poem says God's lovers differ sharply from those who oppose Him.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The living are believers and the dead are disbelievers.

[WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says God enables His allies—those created for Paradise and protected from disbelief—to hear.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | God lets whomever He wills hear His words so that they take heed and find guidance.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r5] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · السدي | reports | Al-Suddī explains “He makes hear” as “He guides whom He wills.”
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p416/r6] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | Those in graves represent disbelievers: they are like the dead because they are deaf to and do not answer the call to faith.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r8] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The living are believers and the dead are unbelievers; God enables whom He wills to hear and benefit.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:35:18-22/r9] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | The people in graves are unbelievers compared to the dead: just as grave-dwellers do not hear, unbelievers do not hear the message.
[JISHUMI:v8p5839/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قراءة العامة | reports | The general reading has bi-mismaʿ with genitive and nunation, while min is accusative in position.
[JISHUMI:v8p5839/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Ismāʿ is making a sound heard so that it can be perceived.

[JISHUMI:v8p5839/r9] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Samʿ is perceiving what is heard and also means the ear, the organ by which hearing occurs.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r7] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The living and dead mean believers and unbelievers.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#3/r8] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · قيل | reports | Another view takes them to mean scholars and the ignorant.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p418#4/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | God makes whomever He wills hear so that they heed and respond.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Believers are alive and unbelievers dead in that unbelievers fail to understand remembrance or attend to it.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The statement returns the matter of hearing to God’s will.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p435#2/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The verse compares unbelievers with the dead in graves, whose inability to hear is familiar to everyone.

[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عمر وابنه عبد الله | prefers | Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the verse does not contradict the report about the well: God restored the dead men’s spirits to rebuke them; he prefers ʿUmar and his son ʿAbd Allāh’s position, citing the Prophet’s statement that they hear no less than the living.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · عائشة | reports | ʿĀʾisha holds the Prophet did not make the dead hear but meant to reproach the living unbelievers; she used this verse as evidence.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p436/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · الحسن بن أبي الحسن | reports | Al-Ḥasan ibn Abī al-Ḥasan reads bi-masmiʿin with an annexation construction.
[TABRISI:35:18-22/r21] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The living and dead represent believers and unbelievers.
[TABRISI:35:18-22/r22] TABRISI, d. 548 · قيل | reports | Another interpretation is scholars and ignorant people.
[TABRISI:35:18-22/r24] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | God benefits through hearing whomever He wills to favor and guide; this does not deny that unbelievers literally heard His signs.
[TABRISI:35:18-22/r25] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | The Prophet cannot make unbelievers benefit from hearing when they refuse to accept, just as the dead in graves cannot hear.
[TABRISI:35:18-22/r3] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | To make someone hear is to bring about an audible sound in a form the hearer can perceive.

 person is described as alive.

[RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | After contrasting guidance and misguidance, al-Razi identifies the believer as seeing the clear path and the unbeliever as blind.
[RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The blind and seeing represent believer and unbeliever; darkness and light represent unbelief and faith, with the unbeliever burdened by blindness as well as darkness.
[RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The living and dead are another comparison: a blind person shares some perception with the seeing, but an unbeliever has no beneficial perception and is like the dead; the repeated verb sets this image apart.
[RAZI-FULL:v26p15/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Negation repeats where the contrasts are strongest: darkness and light, and shade and heat, are direct opposites; life and death differ more essentially than seeing and blindness, so the final contrast also merits emphasis.
[RAZI-FULL:v26p16#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Living and dead are plural because the gap is absolute: no dead person equals any living person in perception, whether kinds or individuals are compared.
[RAZI-FULL:v26p16/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The living are believers who accepted God's revelation; the dead are those who heard clear verses but gained no benefit, and are placed after the believers because their spiritual death followed the believers' life.
[RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | One possible reading contrasts divine and prophetic hearing: God can make the dead hear, while the Prophet cannot make buried people hear; the disbelievers likewise cannot hear his recitation and revelation.
[RAZI-FULL:v26p17/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Alternatively, the verse consoles Muhammad: only God can make them hear, even if they were deaf rocks, so he bears no responsibility for their response.
[QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r15] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · ابن قتيبة | reports | Ibn Qutayba identifies the living as rational and the dead as ignorant.
[QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r16] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says these are comparisons: just as the pairs differ, believer and unbeliever differ.
[QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r17] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | God enables His people to hear; grave-dwellers are unbelievers whose hearts disbelief has killed.
[QURTUBI-FULL:35:19-22/r18] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الحسن وعيسى الثقفي وعمرو بن ميمون | reports | They read without tanwin for ease; unbelievers resemble grave-dwellers who neither benefit from nor accept what they hear.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Living and dead again represent believers and unbelievers, a stronger comparison hence repeated verb; alternatively, scholars and ignorant people.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r8] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | God enables whomever He wills to understand His signs and take admonition.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:35:19-22/r9] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Calling persistent unbelievers dead extends the metaphor and tells the Prophet to give up hope of making them hear.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The living symbolize those who entered Islam and the dead those who did not.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The extra la strengthens negation; the different waw connections pair some even with even and others odd with odd.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p341#4/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | God knows who will enter Islam and guides whom He wills; the Prophet cannot make the dead hear, since people's fate is hidden from him and he strains over those abandoned to disbelief.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p25/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The majority read الأحياء with masculine agreement, while Zādān from al-Kisāʾī has feminine agreement; the order is eloquent because it moves from believer/unbeliever to their light and final dwelling.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p26/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الرازي | reports | For al-Rāzī, the living are believers who accepted revelation and the dead are those who heard clear signs but gained no benefit; he sees them as later than the believers.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | God's causing people to hear means granting the response that leads to faith; the resistant audience is like the dead in graves because their hearts are dead to truth.

[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p27/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Abū Ḥayyān summarizes al-Rāzī's argument that the living/dead contrast is strongest: no dead person matches a living person's perception.
[SAMIN-DURR:35:19-22/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Both living and dead are plural because their difference is greatest: no dead person equals a living person in perception, comparing kinds or individuals.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p543/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | As the dead disbelievers do not benefit from guidance after death, the Prophet cannot make the doomed polytheists hear or guide them.

[BIQAI-FULL:v6p217/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God gives hearing, meaning guidance, to whom He wills and deafens, blinds, overturns, or ruins whom He wills among living hearts and spirits and dead meanings and forms.

[ITQAN:v3p34/r10] ITQAN, d. 911 · ابن الصائغ | reports | The third purpose is honor: examples put men before women, the free before the enslaved, the living before the dead, and hearing before sight. Ibn ʿAtiyya reports al-Naqqash’s argument that this ordering favors hearing and sight.
